problems: The keystone is a narrow box that only just clears the arch ring, so it reads as a small hook or tab sticking up from the arch instead of a keystone set into it. Make it a wide, tapered wedge that is clearly part of the arch.

The wall, the door surround, the steps and the pavement are all near-white and blend together. The cream stone reads as white, and the steps and surround don't stand out from the wall. Give them distinct, warmer stone tones: a darker cream wall, a lighter surround, and grey-beige steps and pavement.
The skirting strip along the wall runs straight through the steps. Split it so it stops at the steps on each side.

The keystone at the crown of the arch renders as a thin bent spike instead of a solid block. The warp seems to work in the box's unscaled unit coordinates, so p[2]/0.13 overshoots and folds the bottom corners inward. Replaced it with a plain keystone block set into the arch, slightly wider at the top, built as a 4-sided cone so the taper needs no warp.
